item.title: Middle East war live: Israeli strikes put Lebanon's heritage sites in 'serious danger', Beirut says
item.description: Israeli strikes on southern Lebanon are putting heritage sites in “serious danger”, warned Beirut's Minister of Culture Ghassan Salamé. "Bombings fell very close to the ruins of Tyre," he said, while adding that the Beaufort Castle was “directly hit”. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.

item.title: 'More than 100,000 people live in this city': Israel urges Tyre residents to leave homes
item.description: FRANCE 24 correspondent Renée Davis reports from Beirut on the Israeli military's call for the population of Tyre in southern Lebanon to leave their homes ahead of a fresh wave of air strikes.

item.title: Closer to war or to peace? US, Iran near deal on 60-day ceasefire
item.description: The ​United States threatened Thursday to target ally Oman if it helped impose a tolling system in the key Strait of Hormuz, warning of sanctions against all parties involved in such actions. The United States and Iran also accused each other of violating an ongoing truce following an exchange of fire, three months after the Middle East war began with a wave of US-Israeli strikes on the Islamic republic. The latest exchange was the most serious since Washington and Tehran agreed to a ceasefire

item.title: How far have the US and Iran got towards ending the Iran war?
item.description: The United States and Iran have reached ⁠an agreement to extend ​a ceasefire, allow shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and lift a US blockade and some sanctions on Iran, sources told Reuters, but the deal has not been finalised. An agreement would represent a big step towards ending a ​war that has pushed the world towards an energy crisis, though the underlying dispute over Iran's nuclear programme would only be thrashed out in talks over subsequent weeks.

item.title: Netanyahu directs Israeli forces to expand Gaza control to 70 percent
item.description: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Thursday he had directed Israel's military to take more of Gaza, initially by seizing 70% of the Palestinian territory, where the population is already penned into a tiny strip of land along the coast. item.title: US, Iran engage in tit-for-tat attacks
item.description: Iran and the US engaged in tit-for-tat clashes this Thursday. Tehran said it fired on an American army base in the region, while the US claimed it had struck Iran’s Bandar Abbas port. Later in the day, Axios reported that Washington and Tehran had reached an agreement to extend their ceasefire by ​60 ‌days, but that ⁠President Donald Trump has yet to ‌approve it. item.title: 'Tightening the grip': Israeli army to take control of 70 percent of Gaza Strip
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Thursday he had ordered the country's military to take control of 70 percent of the Gaza Strip, in defiance of the terms of a fragile ceasefire that took effect in October. Under the terms of the ceasefire, Israeli forces were to pull back behind a so-called "yellow line", a demarcation between the area under Hamas control and that held by the Israeli army. FRANCE 24's Noga Tarnopolsky reports from Jerusalem.

item.title: Israel launches deadly strike near Beirut, widening Lebanon offensive
item.description: Israel pounded south Lebanon with deadly strikes and widened its offensive with the first raid near Beirut in weeks where authorities said a woman and two children were killed despite a ceasefire. The attack near the capital came after heavy strikes on south Lebanon that authorities said had killed at least 14 people, including three children. The escalation comes as Lebanon and Israel prepare for talks between military delegations at the Pentagon on Friday, and for US-brokered talks early next

item.title: Israel declares new 'combat zone' in southern Lebanon, orders evacuations
item.description: Israel expanded its military campaign in southern Lebanon on Wednesday, ordering residents to evacuate areas south of the Zahrani River as strikes intensified despite an April ceasefire. The escalation comes as Israeli officials seek to pressure Hezbollah while avoiding actions in Beirut that could complicate US-led diplomacy with Iran.

item.title: Israeli strikes kill dozens in southern Lebanon as Netanyahu expands ground campaign
item.description: Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon killed 31 people and wounded 40 on Tuesday, Lebanon’s health ministry said, including at least four children and three women, as Israel said it was intensifying operations despite a truce with the Iran-backed group Hezbollah.
